## Goal-aligned decisions

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.



Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.


This launchpad is the operator's own DotLn instance. Its purpose is to plan and
run bounded, evidence-gated work orders across the operator's repositories, so
that every change arrives as a pull request the operator reads before it merges,
while the kit itself stays upstream and reaches this fork only through starter
updates. The first workstream is DotLn-Angular, an Nx and Angular monorepo that
serves two outcomes at once: the operator's reference Angular workspace, which a
colleague should recognize as the way the operator builds Angular, and the
operator's sandbox app, one app with sub-apps behind a menu: a scene for
authoring game AI from a toolbox mined from the works the operator reads, a
view of DotLn's machinery where a change to an agent's mechanisms shows what
changes in an example use case, the operator's own digital twin, and side
utilities. Every new idea lives there first as a toy the operator plays with
before promoting the ones that work, for the five UIFA roles, people and
software actors alike. The app is not wired to DotLn core: its data comes from
public mining into its own store, served to the UI through its own API, and it
informs the platform through GitHub issues, never by writing a control record,
so that the app improves the platform, the platform the starter, the starter
this fork, and the fork the app in turn. The critical path runs from registering
that repository in this launchpad, through one witnessed target order that
scaffolds the workspace, to a foundation where a feature is added by convention:
shared libraries, the component taxonomy, events and stores, the sub-app shell,
and a legitimate client-side authentication and permission model. Later
workstreams join the same way: one registration and one planning pass each,
with the fork's own machinery changes cut as self orders beside them.

Escalation: eleven paid refutations do not themselves justify further judgments or a larger certification program. Success to the successful: the client port preserves provider separation; no evidence establishes that credible library alternatives were excluded. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: single-flight refresh and explicit failure transitions reduce manual session rescue. Rule beating: inspecting issued tokens across browser stores strengthens grep checks, while the controlled mock limits interoperability evidence. Seeking the wrong goal: this is a named foundation outcome, not authentication added to gate otherwise public toys.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost explicitly removes nothing and adds code plus a runtime client dependency. Closing the declared foundation gate supplies a concrete investment rationale, but does not establish a removal larger than the addition.
orders.failureBehavior: Public behavior degrades explicitly: null auth configuration admits the four public routes and renders unavailable login. Refresh failure signs out, invalid credentials fail, and missing permission denies protected access. Those are intended security outcomes; restoring anonymous protected access would defeat the mechanism. The mocked walkthrough and production exclusion are explicitly separated.

findings.reason: A jointly controlled mocked provider demonstrates the bounded client flow, but does not establish configuration-only interoperability with another provider. This integration limit does not require adding a real provider to this order or withholding the foundation work.
findings.reopenWhen: A later authorized integration with a conforming provider requires Angular code changes because issuer behavior was hard-coded rather than configured behind the port.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Consumes WO-016's records/replay libraries and WO-008's authentication; it does not close another foundation prerequisite. It delivers the operator's result-based patience experiment. NoOp leaves the replay comparison, parameter flips and retained executable variants unavailable. No quantified cost of foregoing the experiment is recorded.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: presentation-only replay, browser-only persistence and no shipped wait policy preserve platform authority. Tragedy of the commons: approximately fifty-five files, 170 KB, fifteen steps, 6–9 hours and permanently retained variants create cumulative costs; lazy chunks bound loading, not total history. Drift to low performance: baseline reproduction and replayed readiness constrain the result model. Escalation: five paid refutations and two new commands add process costs without proving recurring value. Success to the successful: multiple retained variants permit alternatives, although permanence increases maintenance. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: corrupt state falls back automatically, but missing-base checking requires an operator fetch. Rule beating: baseline equality does not alone validate counterfactual results; shifted-completion tests address part of that risk. Seeking the wrong goal: close time, waiting and early fires replace agreement with operator beats as the explicit standard.
orders.removalBalance: No. Nothing is removed, and old variants are deliberately retained forever. Potential improvement in future waiting is an experimental benefit; this order ships no platform wait policy and records no realized saving.
orders.failureBehavior: Runtime persistence failures explicitly fall back to the first registry entry without flips. The registry check deliberately refuses a missing base commit and requests a fetch, so the mechanism is not universally fail-open. Preserving historical immutability explains that refusal, but does not establish its operational cost or availability of unaffected replay.

findings.reason: The missing-base refusal protects against silently accepting rewritten variants, but introduces a concrete operator repair dependency. It is a known tradeoff, not an observed failure or a reason to weaken immutability.
findings.reopenWhen: Ordinary supported checkouts repeatedly require manual fetch rescue, or the missing historical base prevents viewing an otherwise valid unchanged baseline.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Delivers public mining and the shelf used to choose a next toy; it does not unblock the authentication foundation gate or build the six proposed toys. NoOp leaves the nineteen run designs outside this shelf, the six new designs absent and The Art of War unmined here. The records supply no quantified search, decision or delay cost for that alternative.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: app-owned catalog data and the GitHub-issue graduation route preserve separation from platform controls. Tragedy of the commons: approximately thirty-two source files, 300 data rows, 190 KB, fourteen steps and two fan-outs require aggregate worker accounting beyond the 4–6-hour estimate. Drift to low performance: full-design source equality, readable pages and linked tools establish more than a toy count. Escalation: building the six toys and issue export remain excluded, limiting scope growth. Success to the successful: six sources absent from the original toy set receive designs rather than being excluded by prior investment. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: the shelf should reduce reconstruction of buried designs, while new command and data maintenance remain costs. Rule beating: source hashes and mutation tests strengthen fidelity; no-read declarations cannot establish provenance where reads are unobserved. Seeking the wrong goal: choosing a useful next toy is the outcome, not twenty-five cards or additional mining rows.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost explicitly removes nothing. Consolidating existing designs may remove repeated searching and reconstruction, but no saving is measured against the added shelf, schemas, checks and data.
orders.failureBehavior: The provenance record explicitly permits unobserved read logging, avoiding refusal solely because a host lacks attributable observations. Unknown tool ids and changed imports intentionally fail validation. Runtime fallback from malformed new catalog or toy data to the existing catalog and scene is unspecified; no such failure is observed.

findings.reason: A worker's no-read statement plus an unobserved journal honestly records uncertainty, but cannot establish that quarantined material was excluded. It must not be treated as positive observation of a clean provenance boundary.
findings.reopenWhen: An attributable read observation shows a map or toy worker accessed quarantined material despite the accepted no-read statement, or a candidate contains material traceable to that access.
